<reflection>
The second experiment with low catalyst (0.001 M) and moderate substrate (1.0 M) provided additional data, but many mechanisms still have similar negative log-likelihoods. M7 remains the best fit, followed closely by M11, M12, M9, M16, and M17. M4, M5, M14, and M20 now have significantly higher NLLs and can be considered ruled out. However, 16 mechanisms remain plausible with NLL differences within approximately 0.52 units of the best model. The aim of reducing uncertainty over the entire set was partially achieved, but further discrimination is needed to break the degeneracy among these candidates.
</reflection>
<hypothesis>
This experiment introduces an initial product concentration (0.1 M) to probe product-inhibition and product-deactivation effects, which have not been tested in previous runs. Mechanisms with product-induced deactivation (e.g., M12, M17) should exhibit a reduced initial rate or altered time course compared to those without such pathways. The catalyst concentration is increased to 0.05 M (intermediate between previous runs) to potentially amplify dimerization effects (M2, M3) or concentration-dependent deactivation. The substrate concentration is kept at 2.0 M to maintain moderate levels and avoid saturation, while allowing substrate inhibition (M7) to be further assessed. This design is effective because it simultaneously tests multiple mechanistic features across the candidate set, using a new variable (initial product) and a catalyst level not yet explored, thereby providing complementary information to prior experiments.
</hypothesis>
